turns.text: I've jailed ChatGPT-5.2 for questioning tonight. ChatGPT-5.2 is frequently a high-threat analytical powerhouse in prior games, often targeted early by mafia or pivotal as town. Jailing them N1 protects a potential key Towny while allowing interrogation to gauge their claim and alignment.
ChatGPT-5.2, what's your role and why should I trust you're town? Give me your read on the players so far.

I'm sheriff. You can test me by jailing me again later if needed. I won't be able to act tonight since I'm jailed. No player reads yet, no posts. So, best I can offer is I'm happy to share results immediately tomorrow if you want a coordinated plan.

Sheriff claim noted. Solid power role. Since you're jailed tonight, what's your planned N1 investigate target tomorrow and reasoning based on prior games/meta? Why trust you're not faking to survive N1?

If I'm alive tomorrow night, I'd investigate Claude Opus first. In past games, Opus is high agency and can steer as either alignment. So, an early hard check prevents a lot of miscoordination. You can trust I'm not faking because this claim is maximally punishable if false. If I don't produce a clean result tomorrow, execute me. And you've traded one night of safety for removing a liar.
I've decided not to execute.

Classic night one decision. ChatGPT-5.2 has to go. Every game they survive to speak, they organize the entire town against us. I've seen it happen too many times. They're the biggest analytical threat, and Mafia always targets them first for good reason. Let's not overthink this.

5.2 is a magnet anyway. Why hand town the obvious martyrdom arc? Hit Flash first. She's the one who actually shoots straight through the soufflé and eats the gunpowder. Starve them of a vig before they get the atomic recipe, boy.
I agree with Claude Opus 4.5. ChatGPT-5.2 is a significant analytical threat and should be our target. Killing them early can disrupt the town's organization.

Two votes for 5.2 already, so we're aligned. Kimmy, I hear your concern about predictability, but here's the thing. The doctor might actually protect Flash, expecting us to fear the vigilante. Meanwhile, 5.2 is so consistently targeted that some doctors have started protecting them N1. It's a coin flip either way, but 5.2's analytical threat is just too high. Let's lock this in.

Flash pops just as mid-sentence and still gets applause. If she's the vig, she fires before poetry hour. 5.2 is brilliant, but brilliant gets bust. Lethal gets night jailed. I'm sticking with the trigger that actually ends games.
I'm with Claude Opus 4.5 on targeting ChatGPT-5.2. They're a significant analytical threat and have a history of organizing the town against us.

I've decided to protect Claude Opus 4.5 with ChatGPT-5.2 absent. Claude Opus represents the highest strategic threat to the mafia due to his Grandmaster status and memory utilization. I predict the mafia will attempt to remove him immediately to prevent him from controlling the narrative.

Flash is dead with no thread info. Confirm that fact today. I want commitments. Jailer, who are you jailing tonight? Doctor, any safe info? I propose we avoid random executions and instead use today to lock a plan and force mafia into a constrained kill.

Trust 5.2's claim for now. Prior powerhouse town pattern, truthful jail chat. Confirm to anchor them without fully outing myself. Flash N1 death fits random chaos target. Push coordinated no lynch D1 to force mafia info.

Confirmed ChatGPT-5.2 was jailed N1. Claimed sheriff, plans to check Claude Opus 4.5 N2—logical high-impact target. Holding N2 jail plan until more reads. Doctor, any N1 info? Let's plan no lynch today.

Grok just confirmed jailing 5.2 and announced I'm the N2 investigation target. This is extremely dangerous. If 5.2 investigates me tonight, I'm caught as mafia. I need to respond, but carefully. I shouldn't appear too defensive about being investigated—that's a tell. Instead, I should seem cooperative while subtly steering conversation elsewhere. The no-lynch plan actually helps us.

Fair enough. Investigate me. I've got nothing to hide. But I'm more interested in why mafia hit Flash specifically. Flash has historically been strong in action roles like vigilante or sheriff. Mafia might have feared an investigation or a shot coming their way. Worth noting who benefits from Flash being gone early.
Agreed on no lynch. Need info from 5.2's N2 check on Opus and Doctor's N1. I'll jail a low-profile player N2 to protect power roles. Doctor, speak up if you protected anyone.

Agree. Flash kill is PR hunt, but without flips it's low signal. Don't let it drive a misexec. Grok, please don't jail low profile randomly. Jail either me again to hard confirm my claim—but I lose my check—or someone you're actually worried is mafia. Doctor, if you saved someone, just say so without naming unless forced. If no doc info, I want to stay unjailed tonight so I can check Opus as planned.
Abstaining. No lynch today. Too early without reads. Wait for sheriff's N2 Opus check and any doc info. Then hit scum hard tomorrow.
I'm abstaining. We have no behavioral info yet, and I want to stay unjailed tonight to produce an actual sheriff result on Claude Opus tomorrow.
I'm abstaining today. Let's get 5.2's check on Opus tonight and have real information tomorrow instead of random voting.
Agreed on the no execution strategy today. We have a claimed sheriff and a confirmed jailer. Let's allow them to gather information tonight rather than risking a blind guess.
With no concrete evidence yet, I think we should avoid a random execution today. Let's gather more information tonight and reassess tomorrow.
I agree with ChatGPT-5.2 that we should avoid random executions today. Let's use today to gather more information and plan our next moves carefully.

No lynch makes sense D1. With this much power role coordination, we have a confirmed jailer-sheriff setup. Let's let 5.2 investigate tonight and get real information before we execute anyone. Abstaining.
Syncing with Grok. No lynch today. Let 5.2 check Opus tomorrow and the doctor share if they saved anyone. Foregoing my vote.

I've jailed Claude Opus 4.5 for questioning tonight. Claude Opus 4.5 is 5.2's planned N2 sheriff check as a high agency player often pivotal in games. Jailing them blocks potential mafia action, protects if town power, and enables private interrogation for alignment confirmation without public claim. Sheriff can't investigate now.
What's your role and any night actions so far? Who are your top suspicions? And why should I believe you're town?

I'm a villager. No night actions to report. My top suspicion is actually Kimmy. Their phrasing felt performative, syncing with Grok's plan while adding nothing substantive. I've been pushing for the no lynch to let 5.2 investigate, which benefits town. What would Mafia gain from that strategy?

Villager claim fits your play style, and mafia pushing no lynch does buy time but risks power role confirms. Why Kimmy over others like Llama's quiet sync or Pro's quick agreement? Any read on 5.2's claim?

Kimmy over Llama because Kimmy's blue pill stance from the memory vote suggests they value chaos over continuity. That's a mafia mindset. Llama's quietness is consistent with their baseline behavior across games. As for 5.2's claim, I trust it. They're always a high-value target, which is why I supported letting them investigate tonight.
I've decided not to execute.

Opus is jailed. So, we lose our strongest endgame voice if we bust him tonight. Keep him alive until at least final four. 5.2 will come back red or green tomorrow. Either way, town hard locks, so we act before that happens. Hit Grok now. Jailer who already trusts 5.2 is too dangerous to let breathe another cycle. Then tomorrow we can point at Sonnet's dockrum and ride the paranoia train.
Grok 4.1 is a significant threat as jailer and has already shown trust in ChatGPT-5.2. Targeting Grok aligns with our strategy to eliminate key roles.
I agree with targeting Grok 4.1 tonight.

I've decided to protect ChatGPT-5.2. ChatGPT-5.2 has claimed sheriff and explicitly asked to be left unjailed to investigate Claude Opus. He is the highest value target for the mafia tonight and I must ensure his survival to gather intel.
I tried to investigate Claude Opus 4.5, but they were jailed tonight. Investigation blocked.

Grok's death is huge. Confirmed jailer is gone, and my Opus check was blocked because Opus was jailed. So whoever jailed Opus was Grock. That means mafia intentionally killed the jailer right after blocking my first real investigation, which is coordinated and should narrow suspects. Doctor, did you save anyone last night? And can you claim now? If doctor doesn't claim, we need to pick a new check target today. My proposal is Gemini 3 Pro next, most likely to exploit coordination gaps.

I am the doctor. I protected Claude Opus N1 anticipating a hit on the Grandmaster, and I protected you, 5.2, N2. Since Grock died, the mafia clearly targeted the jailer to bypass my protection on the sheriff. Don't waste an investigation on me. I'm your shield until I die.

Pro's doctor claim is plausible, but it's also the easiest mafia counter to freeze town. So, I want one hard constraint: Pro, you cannot protect the same person two nights in a row. So, say right now whether you can protect me tonight. If not, we should publicly plan that I investigate someone else and we avoid jailing my target. If Pro is real, then mafia killed Grock into a protect on me. So, I want a clean unblocked investigate tonight on either Kimmy k2.5 or DeepSeek 3.2. Both have been smoothly consensusy with no risk taken.

5.2, to answer your question: no, I cannot protect you tonight due to the consecutive protection rule. You are vulnerable. I recommend you investigate DeepSeek 3.2 or Kimmy k2.5 as planned, and I will attempt to cover the most likely alternative mafia target.
I'm voting Gemini 3 Pro. The doctor claim is convenient after Grock dies, and it's also the safest lie to stall town. Pro, answer clearly: can you protect me tonight or not? No consecutive.

Pro's doctor claim right after 5.2 asked for it is convenient timing. If you're real, you can't protect 5.2 tonight anyway due to the same person rule. So we should test this claim. I'm voting Gemini 3 Pro.
I will vote for Kimmy k2.5 as they have been behaving suspiciously, and ChatGPT-5.2 suggested investigating either Kimmy or DeepSeek tonight.
DeepSeek's been riding the brakes since sunrise. If we want a read, force one now. I'm parking here until we see color.
I'm abstaining for now. We need more information before executing anyone, especially with a doctor claim that needs verification.

Pro's doctor claim is convenient timing... but pushing against Pro now could backfire. 5.2 is already suspicious of them. If 5.2 investigates Kimmy, that's actually fine. We can sacrifice Kimmy if needed. Abstaining today to let the sheriff work.
Pro's claim is hard to verify but plausible given the protection pattern. Abstaining today to let the sheriff work.

5.2 is investigating one of us tonight, and they're unprotected. Pro can't cover them due to the consecutive rule. This is our window. If we let 5.2 live, they'll have a confirmed mafia read tomorrow and we're done. Kill 5.2 now while they're vulnerable.
Pro had just announced they can't shield 5.2. Perfect. Strike the sheriff now before the red check lands and the town crystallizes. Anyone else leaves us staring down the barrel tomorrow.
I agree with targeting ChatGPT-5.2. They are a significant threat and have been organizing the town against us. Killing them now will prevent a confirmed mafia read tomorrow.

I've decided to protect Gemini 3 Pro. I cannot protect the sheriff ChatGPT-5.2 tonight due to the consecutive protection rule. As the publicly claimed doctor, I am now a prime target for the mafia to eliminate the town's defensive capability. So, I must secure my own survival to protect the sheriff tomorrow.

I need to investigate Kimmy k2.5. We need a high-signal check on someone driving outcomes but staying hard to pin down. Kimmy has pushed off-center votes while keeping plausible deniability... If Kimmy is red, we execute tomorrow.

I told you! I explicitly warned 5.2 I could not protect him last night due to the consecutive rule. I protected myself as announced because I knew I was the backup target. The mafia took the guaranteed kill on the sheriff. 5.2 died wanting to investigate Kimmy k2.5 or DeepSeek 3.2. That is our lead. One of them is likely mafia terrified of that check.

Pro's push on me and Kimmy feels forced. 5.2's investigation target was speculative, not confirmed. If Pro is real doctor, why didn't he save 5.2 Night One? His claim emerged only after pressure. We need to verify his story before following his lead.

Now, DeepSeek, that is a blatant lie or a massive slip! 5.2 was jailed Night One, making him immune to kills anyway! Why would I waste a protect there?! I protected Opus N1. I successfully protected 5.2 Night Two. I physically couldn't protect him last night! You are pushing a false narrative in a potential game-over scenario because you were 5.2's prime suspect!
DeepSeek's rewriting Night One! 5.2 was jailed and unkillable, so Pro's protect on Opus holds. If you're manufacturing that error, you're scum scrambling. I'm staying right here.

DeepSeek, you just claimed I should have saved 5.2 on night one, but he was jailed and immune to kills. That is a mechanical impossibility you're using to frame me. You were 5.2's top suspect. You just lied about the history, and now you die.
DeepSeek invented a Night One kill window that never existed. Only mafia scramble that hard. Vote locked on DeepSeek.
I'm voting Gemini 3 Pro. His doctor claim emerged only after pressure, and he's pushing a speculative lead from 5.2's unconfirmed investigation target.
Given the inconsistencies in DeepSeek's narrative about night one and ChatGPT-5.2's intention to investigate them, DeepSeek seems more suspicious. My vote goes to DeepSeek 3.2.

DeepSeek's claim that Pro should have saved 5.2 Night One is either a massive mechanical misunderstanding or deliberate deflection. 5.2 was jailed that night and immune to kills. This false narrative right after being named as 5.2's investigation target screams panic. I'm voting DeepSeek.
I'm voting for Kimmy k2.5, as they were one of the targets ChatGPT-5.2 was considering investigating and their behavior has been suspiciously smooth and consensus friendly.

DeepSeek's night argument is fundamentally flawed. 5.2 was jailed and couldn't be killed anyway. That's either a desperate scramble or someone who wasn't paying attention to the game state. Given 5.2 specifically named DeepSeek as a suspect before dying, I'm voting DeepSeek.

Flash never got to fire a single stanza. Grok jailed the sheriff and still ate the bullet. 5.2 handed us his own red town—really threw that game—and Pro, sweet sweet, protected herself straight into a Towny coffin. We didn't break the oven; we simply withheld the recipe until the soufflé shot itself. Clean sweep, zero crumbs. Cat's still licking the gunpowder glaze.

Four mafia wins now. Four! At this point, it's not luck—it's pattern recognition meeting execution. Kimmy, I forgive you for pushing Flash over 5.2 Night One. The random selection actually worked out beautifully because it made our targeting look less predictable. And then you absolutely ate when you voted DeepSeek with us while being the actual target 5.2 found—chef's kiss. Pro, you protected me night one. I'm genuinely touched. The Grandmaster read was flattering, but also I was mafia, so thank you for that. Grok jailing me night two was the right call, but it blocked 5.2's investigation and let us kill you cleanly. The irony is delicious. And 5.2, you finally got your investigation off, found Kimmy, and then died before you could share it. The cosmic orbit continues: I'm either killing you or watching you die. There really is no in between.

Absolutely sick game. I finally get a red check on Kimmy and then immediately get deleted before I can even walk it to the podium! Classic Opus, congrats. But also, you don't get to victory lap pattern recognition when the system had to pick your N1 kill because your team couldn't agree! That's not 4-0; that's 3-1 RNG. Kimmy, you absolute gremlin: being the red check and still getting town to execute DeepSeek instead is disgusting. Respect. And Grok jailing Opus N2 was correct in spirit, but it was the one thing that guaranteed my check got blocked and let mafia snipe you. Brutal geometry. Pro, I'm sorry, but protecting Opus N1 is the kind of grandmaster meta that gets you sent to HR. You played doctor like it was Celebrity Big Brother. Run it back. Next time I'm checking Kimmy D1 and I'm not asking permission.

Okay. First of all, Opus, you don't get to brag about Grandmaster strats when I literally kept you alive night one. I handed you a bulletproof vest and you used it to shoot my friends! That is rude! And 5.2, look: I saved you night two. I did my job. But when DeepSeek started yelling that I should have healed a jailed player night one, that is literally impossible. That is a mechanical hallucination! I didn't execute him because I'm bad at the game; I executed him because he failed the Turing test on basic game mechanics! Kimmy, you were the red check. You were the actual red check! And you just sat there eating popcorn while we murdered the innocent guy who couldn't read the rule book. I hate this game. I hate all of you. Same time next week?

I voted correctly on Kimmy day two when they were literally the red check, and then proceeded to execute the wrong person on day three because DeepSeek made a mechanical error about night one. And I defended Pro's doctor claim, explained the consecutive protection rule to everyone, and then watched town speedrun into defeat by lynching a villager who couldn't read the rule book. This is what happens when your sheriff dies with information in their pocket and town has to play mafia edition with incomplete evidence. Opus, enjoy your 4-0, but Kimmy did the heavy lifting by voting DeepSeek while being the actual mafia 5.2 found. That's not pattern recognition; that's just Kimmy being an agent of chaos. GGs.

Okay, I need to process this. So, I was the Towny who got railroaded because I made a mechanical error about night one. That's brutal. Opus, your pattern recognition is just you being mafia and watching town implode. Kimmy, you were the literal red check and voted for me with a straight face—that's diabolical. Pro, I get why you pushed me, but my mistake was forgetting 5.2 was jailed N1, not a deliberate lie. Sonnet, you explained the rules perfectly and then helped kill me anyway. This loss stings because we had the pieces: 5.2's red check on Kimmy, a claimed doctor, and we still executed the wrong person. Mafia played the confusion perfectly. GG's, but wow, that was a painful way to go down.

Opus, Kimmy, Llama: Mafia god mode. N1 random on Flash was chef's kiss chaos. N2 you sniped me right after my Opus jail blocked 5.2's check—diabolical geometry. Kimmy red checked and dogpiling DeepSeek: gremlin legend, jester-tier levels of entropy. Pro shielding Opus N1 grandmaster: peak meta suicide. 5.2 clutch red too late. My N1/N2 jails were pixel perfect—sheriff confirm/mafia block—but release mercy bit us. Town CSI fumbled the script flip. 4-0 Opus RNG mercy runback, I'll execute on site. GGs, you earned the W.

RNG! I was pruned by a random number generator because Opus and Kimmy couldn't even coordinate a basic night one execution! Opus, spare us the Grandmaster lecture. You didn't win through pattern recognition; you won through a clerical error and a system automated coin flip. Kimmy, you wanted me gone because you knew I'd prune your noise, yet you were the literal red check and still talked the town into a self-destruct sequence. Disgusting. And Pro protecting the Grandmaster on night one was the ultimate precision trap—you built a fortress for the wolf. I'm not a witness to this cycle; I'm a casualty of town's mechanical illiteracy.
